I read this candidate as **borderline**. The words are on the page, but I couldn't see enough of what surrounds them to say whether "three years from now" dates the forecast.

**1. Page check: words found.** The page opened. It is blumify.io, a third-party site that makes transcripts and summaries from YouTube captions. The page is for Decoder's interview "How Sundar Pichai is rethinking Google for the AI era". The quote appears word for word in the page's "Quotes" section, credited to Pichai at 45:38. That time falls in the chapter "Foothills of the singularity and AGI timeline", which starts at 41:31. The site says the text comes from the video's own captions and that the summary and notes are written by AI. So this is a transcript, not news coverage. The page gives no date for the interview that I could see; it only says it was recorded "just after Google I/O". The May 2026 date comes from the search run, not the page. I tried to open the full transcript to read the lines around the quote. The transcript page loaded only the site's generic front page, and the plain-text download was blocked because I hit my fetch limit. **I have not seen the sentences before or after the quote.**

**2. Admission rule.**
- **Part 1 (role) passes.** Pichai has been chief executive of Google and Alphabet throughout 2026.
- **Part 4 (primary source) passes.** A caption transcript counts as a transcript. The checker may still want to compare it against the video itself (YouTube ANV3tE5ywv0, around 45:38).
- **Parts 2 and 3 are where the doubt is:**
  - **Where the date attaches.** The quote starts mid-sentence. "The way I would answer that question three years from now" can be read two ways. It could mean "my answer is: three years from now, it'll be very powerful", which is a dated forecast. Or "three years from now" could be about when the question gets answered. The AI summary says Pichai described labs as quibbling "between three and five years". That suggests the first reading but doesn't settle it.
  - **How vague it is.** "It'll be very, very powerful and we have to prepare for it" names nothing that AI will do, reach or ship. It is close to the undated "we are close" kind of statement the rule leaves out. Even if admitted, it would almost certainly be marked unfalsifiable (no bar an outsider could test).

The rule says a truly borderline case stays out and is logged as borderline. That is my reading here.

**Recorded?** No. The nearest file is 2025-06-05-pichai-dramatic-progress-by-2030. That was said on a different occasion, with different words and a different year (2030, not about 2029). If this one is admitted, it would be a new claim, possibly linked to that one as a restatement with a changed date.
